## Problem

Let

$$
u(x)=|x|,
\qquad
x\in\mathbb R.
$$

Compute the second derivative of $u$ in the sense of distributions.

## Solution

Since

$$
u(x)=|x|\in L_{\mathrm{loc}}^1(\mathbb R),
$$

it defines a distribution on $\mathbb R$.

We claim that

$$
\boxed{
u''=2\delta_0
}
$$

in the sense of distributions.

Let

$$
\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R).
$$

By the definition of the second distributional derivative,

$$
\langle u'',\varphi\rangle
=
\langle u,\varphi''\rangle.
$$

Thus

$$
\langle u'',\varphi\rangle
=
\int_{\mathbb R}|x|\varphi''(x)\,dx.
$$

Split the integral at the origin:

$$
\langle u'',\varphi\rangle
=
\int_{-\infty}^0(-x)\varphi''(x)\,dx
+
\int_0^\infty x\varphi''(x)\,dx.
$$

For the first integral, integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\int_{-\infty}^0(-x)\varphi''(x)\,dx
&=
\left[(-x)\varphi'(x)\right]_{-\infty}^0
+
\int_{-\infty}^0\varphi'(x)\,dx\\
&=
\varphi(0).
\end{aligned}
$$

Here the boundary term vanishes because $\varphi$ has compact support.

Similarly,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\int_0^\infty x\varphi''(x)\,dx
&=
\left[x\varphi'(x)\right]_0^\infty
-
\int_0^\infty\varphi'(x)\,dx\\
&=
\varphi(0).
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\langle u'',\varphi\rangle
=
2\varphi(0).
$$

But

$$
\langle\delta_0,\varphi\rangle
=
\varphi(0),
$$

so

$$
\langle u'',\varphi\rangle
=
\langle2\delta_0,\varphi\rangle.
$$

Since this holds for every

$$
\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R),
$$

we conclude that

$$
\boxed{
\frac{d^2}{dx^2}|x|
=
2\delta_0
\quad\text{in }\mathcal D'(\mathbb R).
}
$$

## Remark

Classically,

$$
u'(x)
=
\begin{cases}
-1, & x<0,\\
1, & x>0.
\end{cases}
$$

Thus, in the sense of distributions,

$$
u'
=
\operatorname{sgn}(x).
$$

The function $\operatorname{sgn}(x)$ has a jump of size

$$
1-(-1)=2
$$

at the origin. Its distributional derivative is therefore

$$
(\operatorname{sgn}x)'
=
2\delta_0.
$$

Hence one may also summarize the calculation as

$$
|x|'
=
\operatorname{sgn}(x),
\qquad
|x|''
=
2\delta_0.
$$

This is a basic example showing that distributional differentiation detects jump discontinuities through Dirac masses.
